title: API registry search by capability (foundational)
description: Signature original: Documented APIs are registered with their endpoints, methods, and capability tags, and discovery searches this registry by the task's required capability. Only documented, registered APIs are discoverable; undocumented endpoints are invisible by design. The registry is the system's allowlist for external calls. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
registry = [{'name': 'archive-search', 'caps': ['search', 'retrieve'], 'base': 'https://api.example/v1'}]
need = 'search'
hits = [a for a in registry if need in a['caps']]
print('discovered:', [h['name'] for h in hits])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for API Discovery and Invocation Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Input validation against endpoint schema (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before any call, inputs are validated against the endpoint's declared schema: types, required fields, and value ranges. Validation happens client-side so malformed calls never leave the system. A call that fails validation is rejected with the specific schema violation, not attempted hopefully. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Authorization scoping per call (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each invocation carries only the authorization scope its endpoint requires, following the principle of least privilege. Scopes are checked before the call is built, so an over-scoped request is refused locally. Narrow scoping limits the blast radius if any single call is compromised. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for API Discovery and Invocation Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Invocation with bounded retry (foundational)
description: Signature original: Calls execute with exponential-backoff retry on transient failures, capped at a small retry count. Backoff starts at one second and doubles, which is gentle on struggling services. Non-transient errors like 400s fail immediately without retry, because retrying a bad request is just a slower failure. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import time
attempts, max_tries, wait = 0, 3, 0.01
while attempts < max_tries:
    attempts += 1
    ok = attempts == 3  # transient failure twice
    if ok: break
    time.sleep(wait); wait *= 2
print('succeeded on attempt', attempts)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for API Discovery and Invocation Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Response contract checking (foundational)
description: Signature original: Responses are checked against the endpoint's declared response contract before the data is used. A response that parses but violates the contract, such as a missing required field, is treated as a failure of the call, not as usable data. Contract checking catches API drift before it corrupts downstream reasoning. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for API Discovery and Invocation Manager, 2026-10-21.
